This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 21.09.2020 at about 12.45 a.m, when the petitioner was travelling in KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA- 42-F-1827 as passenger from Bengaluru to Kaduru, when it was proceeding at NH-206, near Prakruthi Daba, Nittur, Gadde Bayalu, at that time the driver of KSRTC Bus drove the bus in rash and negligent manner, with high speed and hit the parked Lorry (Tipper) bearing No.KA-52-A-1377 to its backside.
Due to this the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Gubbi Government hospital, Tumakuru District, wherein after first aid he was shifted to Vijayanagar hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery and further went to HOSMAT hospital,
Bengaluru, for further better treatment and took treatment on OPD basis and once again admitted to same hospital as inpatient and has (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 undergone surgery.

The petitioner has spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards hospital and medical expenses and Rs.1,00,000/- towards food, fruits, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges and respondent No.1 has paid Rs.4,00,000/- towards his medical expenses directly to the Vijayanagar hospital on 09.10.2020 by way of cheque and except the said amount, the petitioner Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33214437/
2 has not received any amount and the remaining expenses was borne by the petitioner alone.
The petitioner prior to accident was hale and healthy and was aged about 50 years and doing business of selling tender coconut in Bengaluru and earning Rs.2,000/- per day.

Due to the accident he is not able to do his business and hence,
he was unemployed and facing lot of financial crisis.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of KSRTC Bus and negligent parking of Tipper Lorry.
Even a criminal case is registered against the said drivers of KSRTC Bus and Tipper Lorry.

The respondents No.1 and 2 are the owner and internal insurer of KSRTC Bus and respondents No.3 and 4 are the insurer and owner of the Tipper Lorry, all are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- to the petitioner together with interest at the rate of 12% p.a with costs.
On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 3 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondents No.2 and 4 did not appeared and hence, they were placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denies that there was any rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the K.S.R.T.C Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1827 and alleged accident and as a consequence of which the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and further contended that the bus was on its schedule trip from Bangalore to Shivamogga and the bus was being driven by its driver slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and while it was so proceeding near Prakruthi Daba, Nittur Gaddebayalu.

at about 1.15 a.m, a Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-l377 was so parked due to mechanical defect in the middle of the road,
without displaying any signal and there was raining and when the things stood thus,
a private bus was coming from the opposite side, with bright light and due to bright from the opposite side, tipper lorry was not visible till the bus reached near the tipper lorry.

When the driver (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 of the bus noticed the tipper lorry stopped in the middle of the road without parking light, immediately stopped the bus and in that process it came in contact with the said tipper lorry.

The tipper lorry had no parking lights nor reflectors fitted, further no warning devices were fitted to the vehicle and no top lights on the rear side of the parked vehicle and no road barricade was put around the tipper lorry.
The unattended tipper lorry was so left in the dark night and it was parked in the middle of the road negligently, in flagrant violation of the traffic rules and regulations.
As such for the alleged accident the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-l377 was wholly and solely responsible.
But neither the bus in question not its driver responsible for the accident.

However, the petitioner with an sole intention to make a wrongful gain from this respondent also, falsely implicated the bus in question and foisted a false case against this respondent and further Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33214437/
3 contended that this respondent immediately after the accident has paid a sum of Rs.14,54,004/- to the petitioner towards medical expenses as an ex-gratia.
If this Court was pass an award and Judgment against this respondent, the aforesaid amount kindly be deducted in the Judgment and award.

If this Court holds (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 contributory or sole negligence of lorry driver, in that case the respondents No 3 and 4 shall be directed to refund medical expenses of Rs.14,54,004/- paid by this respondent to the petitioner.
The accident took place due to the negligence of the driver of the tipper lorry by parking the lorry in the middle of the road negligently in flagrant violation of traffic rules and regulations.

But colluding with the Police the petitioner has got the case registered as against the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1827 to make the claim and enrich himself unlawfully and has further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of the KSRTC Bus, age, occupation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and hence pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent is the insurer of Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-1377 and liability to indemnify the respondent No.4 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the driver of the Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1827 was solely responsible for (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 the accident, who hit the Lorry bearing No. KA-52-A-1377 from behind, infact the driver of the Lorry was no way responsible for the injuries and the driver of the Lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving licence and the vehicle was plying without having valid Permit as on the date of accident, thereby, the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and this respondent denies the occurrence and mode of the accident and also actionable negligence of Lorry bearing No. KA-52-A-1377 and also denies manner and occurrence of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, age, occupation, income of the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant.

Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.3.
06.

On going through the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that he sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 21.09.2020 at about 12.45 a.m, on NH-206, near Prakruthi Daba, Nittur, Gadde Bayalu, due to rash and negligent act of driving of KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1827 and also the negligent parking of the Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-1377, by its drivers as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, recasted Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 50 years and doing business of selling tender coconut in Bengaluru and earning Rs.2,000/- per day and he has spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards hospital and medical (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 expenses and Rs.1,00,000/- towards food, fruits, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges.
Due to the accident he is not able to do his business and hence he lost his income and became permanent disabled.

18. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card and even Aadhaar card to show his exact date of birth.
However, in medical records the age of the petitioner is shown as 52 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 52 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 years is 11.

sentences.text: With regard to his avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2020 to be taken as Rs.14,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.14,500/-.

Hence, considering the evidence of PW.3, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 15%.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Discharge summaries as per Ex.P.9 to 11, which indicates that the petitioner was admitted to Vijayanagar hospital, Bengaluru and HOSMAT hospital, Bengaluru, for treatment due to accidental injuries for 45 days as inpatient.

which indicates that on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony due to grievous injuries sustained.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under this head.
23. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.14,500/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 45 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast four months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.58,000/-
(Rs.14,500 x 4) under this head.
(SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 24. Medical expenses:-

corporation and same is required to be deducted towards share of the compensation has to be paid by the corporation.

25. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that, the the petitioner is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.22,86,163/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.40,000/-) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Out of the said compensation amount, 50% of compensation has been already paid by the respondents No.1 and 2 corporation shall be deducted and remaining 50%
awarded compensation amount (SCCH-3) 33 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 shall be paid by the respondent No.3 Insurance Company of the offending lorry.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

In view of reasons assigned to recasted Issue No.1 and and Issue No.2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.22,86,163/- (Rupees Twenty two lakhs eighty six thousand one hundred and sixty three only) with interest at the rate Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33214437/
13 of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.40,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

Out of the said amount, Rs.11,43,081.50/- has to be deducted towards medical bill amount paid by the respondents No.1 and 2 corporation and remaining amount of Rs.11,43,081.50/- shall be paid by the respondent No.3 Insurance Company.
(SCCH-3) 34 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 The respondent No.3 shall deposit above said compensation amount of Rs.11,43,081.50/- with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
